dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows what it knows about one thing as named facts — an order's number, date and address; a file's size, owner and date; a component's category and status; the settings of an account — and the few figures a screen opens with — how many, how much, how long. It wants every such block drawn the same way: a quiet name, the value that answers it, the names in one column where there is room and above their values where there is not, loose where a person reads and tight where a person scans.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a description list reads: per density, the space between two facts, the space between the term column and the value column, the text styles of a term and of a value, and the text style of a figure in the stat layout; the colors of a term and of a value; the space between a term and the value under it; the space between two columns of facts and the least width of a column that holds values; the one line between facts and how facts are told apart (a line or a gap, following the system's choice).
rules: A description list presents the facts of one thing: each a name and the value that answers it. Many things that share the same names are a table; text that is read in order, with a term now and then, is prose.

Use layout inline for a block of facts a person looks things up in, stacked where values are long or the names are, and stat for a few figures with their labels. An inline list stacks by itself when it is narrow; do not switch the layout by hand for a small window.
Set columns to the most columns you want, and let the list draw fewer when it is narrow. An inline list is always one column.
Use density compact where a person scans many facts (a side panel, an inspector) and regular where a person reads them.
Write a term as a short name without a colon. Write a value as the person should read it: format numbers, dates and units yourself, and write "None" or "Not set" where a fact has no value.
A value may hold a tag, a link, inline code or a button; the list places it and styles nothing inside it. A fact, a term and a value are never pressed: put a link or a button inside the value.
A figure in the stat layout is text of the surface's color, never primary and never a status color. Say a change in words, with a glyph (a tag whose label says "up 12 %"), never by color alone.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a line or a fill of your own between facts.

separation.$description: How a fact is told from the fact below it. divider: a line of divider.thickness in divider.color between them, with fact.gap on each side of it. gap: fact.gap of empty space and no line. Follows the system's choice; a list's separation prop overrides it (DSL-13). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product rules its blocks of facts with a line while its joined buttons stand apart, or parts both by space: the system-wide choice gives the common answer, and the description list must be able to leave it, because a line between the facts of a record and a line inside a filled control are not the same decision.

color.$description: The line between two facts: the system's one hairline color. Decorative: facts, terms and values are exposed without it.

thickness.$description: The width of the line between two facts.

gap.$description: The space between a fact and the fact below it, per density: once where facts are told apart by space, and on each side of the line where they are told apart by a line. The list has no row height of its own: a fact is as tall as its term and its values.
The space between the term column and the value column while the term sits beside its value, per density.

color.$description: The text of a term, and of a figure's label in the stat layout: secondary content, quieter than the value it names.

typescale.$description: The text of a term, per density: a label, not running text. In the stat layout it is the style of the label under the figure.

gap.$description: The space between a term and the value under it, between a figure and its label, and between two values of one term. Small, so that a term and its values read as one fact.
The space between two columns of facts in the stacked and stat layouts. Larger than term.gap and stack.gap, so that two facts side by side are not read as one.

min-width.$description: The least width of a column that holds values. A list in columns draws only as many columns as are at least this wide (DSL-7); an inline list whose value column would be narrower than this draws its terms above their values instead (DSL-4). It grows with enlarged text (DSL-21).

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product decides how far a value may be squeezed before its facts are rearranged: a block of facts that sits in a wide page, in a side panel and on a phone must go from several columns to one, and from terms beside values to terms above them, at a width the product can set once.

color.$description: The text of a value, and of a figure in the stat layout.

typescale.$description: The text of a value, per density: the interface's running text, as prose sets a description at its medium size.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product opens a screen with a few figures — how many orders, how much revenue, how long a build took — each larger than anything it says about them, and shows the same kind of figure smaller in a card or a side panel.

typescale.$description: The text of a figure in the stat layout, per density: a heading role, because the figure is what the fact is read for. Its label takes term.typescale and its color is value.color.
